title: Notifications
intro: Who hears what, and how. Today notifications are in-app only (15 kinds, the bell): the coordinator had 536 unread, overdue never notifies and admins get none.

questions.question: Besides the in-app bell, which channels should Vaidyx use?

options.label: Phone web push (Recommended)
options.description: Alerts on the phone's lock screen from the browser; needs HTTPS, and on iPhone the app must be added to the home screen.

options.label: Email from the hospital
options.description: Sent through the hospital's mail server; needs its address and IT approval (the server sends no mail today).

options.label: SMS
options.description: Needs an SMS provider and DLT registration (India's sender and template rules), with a cost per message.

options.label: WhatsApp
options.description: Needs a WhatsApp Business account; every message passes through Meta's servers.

questions.why: Today: in-app only; email only as a draft from the doctor's own mail (V2 sections 3 and 13). Treating doctors want notifications on the phone (atlas role needs). The server allows outbound HTTPS, so push, mail, SMS and WhatsApp gateways are reachable.

questions.question: What may a message outside the app show about the patient?

options.label: No patient details (Recommended)
options.description: Only the task and Case File number, for example '1 new request for Radiology'; details open after login.

options.label: UHID and task, no name
options.description: A radiologist can find the study at once; the UHID leaves the hospital in the message.

options.label: Name, UHID and task
options.description: Most useful at a glance; patient identity sits on phones and outside servers.

questions.why: Push, SMS, WhatsApp and email pass through outside servers (R14-Q01). Today the in-app texts carry the patient's name and UHID. Ties to R15 (data leaving the hospital).
questions.skip_if: Skip if R14-Q01 chose no channel outside the app.

questions.question: Should treating-side notifications go to the Case File's own team or to the whole department?

options.label: The Case File team (Recommended)
options.description: The owner doctor and the residents added to that Case File are told; the department sees it only in its lists.

options.label: Whole department, as today
options.description: Every doctor of the owning department hears every event of every Case File.

options.label: Team, copied to the head
options.description: The team is told and the head of department gets a copy.

questions.why: Today notifications are addressed to a department (notify.py), one cause of the flood (U17). Owner's note on G04: the owner is the treating doctor. Settled: the treating doctor adds residents per Case File.

questions.question: When a request reaches a supporting department, who gets the alert?

options.label: Everyone, shows who took it (Recommended)
options.description: All doctors of that department are told; once one acknowledges, the others see it is taken.

options.label: The report's signer, else everyone
options.description: If the HIS names the doctor who signed the report, only that doctor is told.

options.label: The department head only
options.description: The head passes it on; one person per department hears every request.

questions.why: Six supporting departments (settled). Today the department as a whole gets it (bell and inbox). I08 specialist confirmation, requested by the treating doctor, may name a person (R08).
questions.skip_if: Skip if R08-Q04 answered 'Department, first to take' (everyone in the department is then told).

questions.question: What should reach the coordinator as a notification?

options.label: Only what needs them (Recommended)
options.description: Ready marks, late changes before the cut-off and amended values behind a decision; request traffic stays in the readiness list.

options.label: All events of listed Case Files
options.description: Every event of the Case Files listed for a board date.

options.label: Everything, grouped
options.description: As today, but grouped by Case File.

questions.why: U17: the coordinator had 536 unread. Today the coordinator gets case_ready, board_ready, decision_value_changed, the inform-the-patient task and rows addressed to it. The readiness list already shows request states (B15).

questions.question: What should a resident on a Case File be told?

options.label: Same as the owner (Recommended)
options.description: Requests answered, Done, re-fetch results and the decision, only for Case Files they were added to.

options.label: Only tasks given to them
options.description: They hear only what the consultant assigns to them.

options.label: Nothing, they check the app
options.description: The consultant hears everything; residents look in the app themselves.

questions.why: Settled: residents are part of the treating doctor's team per Case File, join with a code, have limited access and cannot sign. Residents usually chase reports (atlas resident role, Hartmann 2026). Their limits are set in R03.
questions.notes: Dropped in validation (17 Oct): same as R06-Q14 (which events reach a resident).

questions.question: Should department and root admins get notifications?

options.label: Admin events only (Recommended)
options.description: Department admin: account or join requests, a doctor's access ending; root admin: hospital system connection down. No patient details.

options.label: Also overdue counts
options.description: The department admin also hears how many of its department's requests are overdue (counts only, no patients).

options.label: No, as today
options.description: Admins check their own screens.

questions.why: G05: admins are blind by design (no clinical access). How accounts and joins are created is R04 and R06.

questions.question: What should board members be told before a session?

options.label: Agenda out, start reminder (Recommended)
options.description: One message when the agenda is final, one 15 minutes before the start with the join code.

options.label: Start reminder only
options.description: One message shortly before the meeting.

options.label: Nothing extra
options.description: The join code message from R11 is all they get.

questions.why: Settled: members join from anywhere, phone too, with a six-digit code; how the code is sent is R11. Victoria framework: agenda out 48 hours before (I06 liked).

questions.question: When a request passes its due date, should Vaidyx notify by itself?

options.label: Yes, department then owner (Recommended)
options.description: The department is told on the due date; if still open next morning, the owner's team and the coordinator are told once.

options.label: Department only, daily
options.description: The department is reminded each morning until it acts.

options.label: No, screens only
options.description: As today: overdue appears only when a page is opened.

questions.why: K09: overdue never notifies; it is worked out only when a page is shown. Reminder timing and escalation are R08; this sets who is told.
questions.skip_if: Skip if R08 already set automatic overdue reminders and who gets them.
questions.notes: Dropped in validation (17 Oct): same as R08-Q08 and R08-Q09 (overdue reminders and escalation).

questions.question: Should people get a daily summary instead of a message for every event?

options.label: Morning digest plus urgent (Recommended)
options.description: One message at 08:00 IST with everything open; only urgent items (decision recorded, session starting) come at once.

options.label: Every event at once
options.description: Each event is its own message, as the bell does today.

options.label: Digest only
options.description: One message a day, nothing in between.

questions.why: U17 flood; I13 (grouped notifications and a daily digest). A digest cuts outside messages without hiding anything from the bell.
questions.skip_if: Skip if R14-Q01 chose no channel outside the app.

questions.question: How should the in-app bell group notifications?

options.label: By Case File (Recommended)
options.description: One line per Case File with its newest event and a count; open it to see all, mark all read per line.

options.label: By kind
options.description: Requests, Done, ready marks and decisions in separate groups.

options.label: Flat list with filters
options.description: Newest first as today, with filters by kind and Case File.

questions.why: U17: 536 unread, no grouping, filter or digest; I13. How the bell looks is R17; this sets the rule.

questions.question: Should messages outside the app pause at night?

options.label: Yes, 21:00 to 07:00 IST (Recommended)
options.description: Held and sent in the morning; each person can change the hours.

options.label: No quiet hours
options.description: Messages go out whenever the event happens.

options.label: Each person sets their own
options.description: No default; nothing pauses until a person sets it.

questions.why: Nothing in Vaidyx is an emergency alert, so board work can wait for the morning. Applies to push, SMS, WhatsApp and email, never to the in-app bell.
questions.skip_if: Skip if R14-Q01 chose no channel outside the app.

questions.question: You liked I15, 'Re-fetch now' inside the Done notification. What should the tap do?

options.label: Re-fetch, show result there (Recommended)
options.description: Pulls the changed records at once and says in the notification what closed and what is still missing.

options.label: Open Case File, then re-fetch
options.description: The tap opens the Case File and runs the re-fetch there.

options.label: Open the Case File only
options.description: The doctor looks first and presses Re-fetch themselves.

questions.why: G21: re-fetch is manual and the owner must remember it after Done; I15 liked. Re-fetch pulls only changed versions, and requests close themselves when the record arrives final and signed (B8).
questions.skip_if: Ask only if R08-Q05 answered 'Manual, one tap in notice'.

questions.question: Can each person switch off kinds of messages?

options.label: Hospital defaults, people mute some (Recommended)
options.description: Root admin sets defaults per role; a person may mute optional kinds, never requests to their department.

options.label: Fixed by the hospital
options.description: Nobody changes their own settings.

options.label: Each person chooses all
options.description: Anyone can turn any kind off, requests included.

questions.why: Per-role defaults keep set-up simple; a must-hear list (requests, decisions on one's own Case Files) stops missed work. Settings screens are R04 and R17.
